argument: As a rebuttal to the previous episode on Meditations, this episode weaves together Nietzsche's and Schopenhauer's separate cases against Stoicism: Nietzsche thinks the Stoics aren't life-affirming enough, while Schopenhauer thinks they are too affirming of worldly things to ever understand the world deeply. Nietzsche argues the Stoics view a universe of becoming in terms of being, contradict themselves by modeling behavior on a nature they call indifferent, and are really exercising their will to power by projecting invented values onto the universe, tranquilizing themselves and writing off the messy, excessive parts of life that fuel self-overcoming. Schopenhauer argues Stoicism is secretly eudaimonistic, an essentially selfish regimen for avoiding suffering that mistakes disconnection for wisdom, misses what suffering teaches, and never discovers the deeper path of freedom from the will through aesthetic contemplation, compassion, and ascetic renunciation.
keyIdeas: Nietzsche traces Stoicism back to a Dekadenz beginning with Socrates and Plato, an obsession with rational order that ignores becoming, emergence, creativity, and instinct in favor of aiming at something static you can finally be.

Nietzsche finds a contradiction in aligning your behavior with nature's indifferents, since nature is either a benevolent rational order worth emulating or indifferent, but not both, and he sees the Stoics as projecting values of their own creation onto the universe through the will to power.

Nietzsche's amor fati loves fate whether it is rational or not, while the Stoics first project a rational metaphysics onto everything and only then love fate because it is rational, a self-tyranny that tranquilizes people and writes off messy stretches of life that could fuel self-overcoming.

A Stoic can reply that Stoicism is a virtue ethics whose real goal is adherence to the virtues, with calm and tranquility only a common byproduct of judging rightly, but Schopenhauer counters that Stoicism's true goal is peace of mind free from suffering, making it eudaimonistic ancient advice rather than morality.

For Schopenhauer true morality begins with compassion, literally suffering with others, and the real answer to suffering is freedom from the will through aesthetic contemplation, compassion, and ascetic renunciation, a whole dimension of life a lifelong Stoic never knows exists.

terms.def: Nietzsche's name for the physiological and cultural decline in Western thinking since Socrates and Plato, marked by over-intellectualizing, weakened drives, and moral judging instead of doing.
The contrast between the Stoics aiming their behavior at something static they can eventually arrive at, and Nietzsche's view of transformation as iterative and constantly unfolding.
Nietzsche's idea that people create values and project them onto the universe, mistaking them for something written into it, which is exactly what he thinks the Stoics do with the rational logos.
Schopenhauer's classification of Stoicism as part of the Hellenistic tradition whose true goal is peace of mind free from suffering, with the virtues merely instrumental to getting there.
Schopenhauer's single, blind, aimless metaphysical force underlying everything, experienced by humans as restless striving that never delivers lasting satisfaction and is the source of suffering.
Schopenhauer's starting point for true morality, a word literally translating to suffering with, meaning internalizing and truly feeling the experience of the other.

anchors: Friedrich Nietzsche thought the Stoics… weren’t life-affirming ENOUGH in their view of the world and so ROBBED themselves of some of the most critical aspects of life…and Arthur Schopenhauer thought that the stoics were TOO life-affirming, of WORLDLY things at least
transformation of ANY type personal or otherwise, is always something that is iterative, it’s CONSTANTLY in a state of unfolding. It’s NOT something you can ARRIVE at

how is it possible…for someone to ALIGN their BEHAVIOR with something indifferent? I mean what are we DOING here? Either… this is a benevolent rational order that we need to be modeling our behavior after… or it’s indifferent.

They are exercising their will to power. They are CREATING a set of values and an ethics that goes along with them. And then they are PROJECTING those values ONTO the UNIVERSE… and MISTAKING them as being written IN to the universe.
So you can see they START… by PROJECTING a METAPHYSICS onto things where everything is rational… and then ONLY from THERE they say to LOVE it… BECAUSE it’s rational.
if this didn’t help you become a better Stoic, the Stoic has to see MOST of this time you spent…as essentially a waste of your life.
the goal ISN’T for a Stoic to have calmness and tranquility at all costs…remember Stoicism is a type of virtue ethics. The REAL goal a Stoic needs to focus on is adherence to the virtues.
the TRUE GOAL of Stoicism for him…IS the inner peace of mind, free from suffering. The virtues, become just things that are instrumental to be able to GET there.
He says maybe Stoicism is something that comes EASIER to ACCEPT, to people that are uninspired to begin with.
devoted practice like this ACTUALLY HELPS the problem, in an area that a practicing Stoic, that never considers anything but Stoicism, will never even know exists.

ALL of this ORIGINATED Nietzsche thought…in people like Socrates and Plato…who started this trend of people being practically OBSESSED with the idea that there MUST be some kind of rational, stable ORDER, to the way that things play out in the universe.
he lumps the Stoics in with what he calls the: improvers of life from the history of philosophy.
the picture of a Stoic sage to him… is something like an old man…sitting around, who is constantly safe, and luke warm, and unambitious about everything
One sits IN the suffering and finds a way through it…the other is constantly trying to FIX the suffering, as though its a defect of human life.
If other people AROUND me are suffering at an emotional level, well look those JUDGMENTS they’re making about their situation are just a matter of IGNORANCE.
Think of how lonliness…can strip away distractions, and bring someone to a place where they come to reflect on their own existence.

they end up suffering TWICE: not only do they suffer for the thing just normally…but then in their attempt to TRAIN themselves to keep CENTERED all the time…they end up adding on a whole OTHER layer of suffering on TOP of the original thing

Greatness often requires EXCESS. Sometimes it requires intense emotions. Sometimes quitting your job out of anger at your boss… puts you on a different path in life where you end up living more fully.
compassion…is WHERE true morality BEGINS for Schopenhauer. FAR from the cosmopolitanism of Stoicism, which he thought was just a rational duty towards others FOR YOURSELF ultimately

when you practice being what he calls a “pure, will-less subject of knowledge”...you’ll find that the SUPER strong URGE you usually have to STRIVE for whatever it is you want…that voice starts to quiet inside of you, just a little.
